items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: The name was Spencer Taylor but everybody called him Mike. And I can't think of all the fellas, they were the Sawmill guys

ctx.x: And who played in the band there?

Well now Mike Taylor had the band in the Bui. The name was Spencer Taylor but everybody called him Mike. And I can't think of all the fellas, they were the Sawmill guys, they called it Sawmill. Yeah. They didn't play until on Sundays you know. Couldn't play no other day. And that fella that came to teach me, Paul Rosi had a band in Baudis Elmo. And a fella named Tooker, I forget, Tooker, real name, but he had the band that raised it, the old men bands. And Johnny Hills, he was the boy that took over the young…

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: They were strictly musicians like Paul Rose and Mike Taylor, Spencer Taylor's name.

ctx.x: What about out in the country? Did they play trumpet pretty much the same as in the city? Did they use the same tricks?

Well, not them days. They didn't. They were strictly musicians like Paul Rose and Mike Taylor, Spencer Taylor's name. They put that music up there and just played parades and things. They didn't play no dance music. They played parades and things. What about half-elvin? Did they do that much in those days?
Well, I did that a lot. Tell me that comes from King Oliver. Tell me King Oliver first one did that.
